memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"Each morning everyone gathered as much as they needed, and when the sun grew
hot, it melted away." - Ex 16:21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
There was a window. Gather in the cool of the morning, or find nothing at all.

For forty years this shaped the rhythm of Israelite life. Before anything else,
before the day's work, before the journey, they went out and gathered what they
needed to live.

It is hard not to see the parallel to our own lives with God. There is a reason
believers across the centuries have found the beginning of the day the natural
time to seek Him. Not because God is only available in the morning, but because
what we do first reveals what we depend on, and because the day tends to fill up
with heat and noise.

Jesus, who had more demands on Him than any of us, rose "very early in the
morning, while it was still dark," and went off to a solitary place to pray
(Mark 1:35).

Let us hold this gently, though. Not everyone's life allows a quiet morning.
Night-shift workers, new parents, carers. God is not legalistic about the clock.
The principle is not the hour; it is gathering before the heat, whenever your
morning is.

But do gather. Manna that was not collected simply melted.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. When in your day do you actually seek God, and is it working?
2. What tends to melt away your intentions before you get to them?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, help me to seek You before the heat of the day. Give me a rhythm that
actually fits my life and holds. Amen.
